entry.title: Physical Combat
entry.summary: Close-range strikes, from quick combinations to heavy blows.
entry.development: Close-range defence and recovery after interrupted attacks are the current focus.
entry.artworkAlt: Footwork, guards, counters and combinations on the ground and in the air. Symbolic technique illustration.

trainingRecord.text: Chamber benchmarks remain 75× gravity for ground rounds, 25× for aerial rounds and 150× for slow conditioning; no higher maximum has been established. Peer sparring and cleanup work developed group awareness. In TL-619, tight counters, accumulated damage and sustained pressure let Zero defeat a stronger Nappa while using the sealed channel. Vegeta remained far beyond him; their following training day focused on recovering after interrupted attacks, using separate channel bouts, closure and rest. Four weeks with Nail and the quarry fight developed aerial reversals, guarded combinations and sustained pressure against injured Brask. Subsequent Vegeta rounds improved close-range defence; he still controls their exchanges.

trainingRecord.text: Deliberate suppression, loaded movement, flight and moving releases are established. King Kai’s instruction improves whole-body transitions and control under strain. Lower-flow channeling is steadier; full output remains strenuous. Ki sensing is now trained separately, with limited relative-output tracking. Neither the channel nor cooperative spirit-energy gathering has permanently absorbed another power into the base. Nail’s month of instruction and the latest King Kai sessions improved movement, transitions and recovery; no new gravity or endurance maximum was established.

trainingRecord.text: Flight is integrated with evasions, compact strikes and spinning kicks against drones. Full-output aerial rounds reached 25× gravity, distinct from 75× ground rounds and 150× slow conditioning. Flight has now been used in the assessment and both Nappa encounters. Long-range endurance remains unmeasured; greater training gravity did not make Zero faster than a much stronger opponent. Flight-assisted reversals and aerial pressure were also used against Brask.

trainingRecord.text: Started with one small shot on Day 22. Chamber practice developed step-release, moving-target fire and short volleys while manoeuvring. Larger shots require an opening and consume more stamina; accuracy remains imperfect. These are ordinary ki attacks, not an acquired named beam or signature technique. In the mission he destroyed the warehouse with an outward release and used contact blasts and concentrated ki at his fingertips. No stable blade was acquired in that fight. During Yamcha’s Raditz fight, a precise shot destroyed the scouter with only superficial burns to Raditz, leaving Yamcha to win his own fight. On Namek, twenty ordinary shots followed preset wide curves; three hit Nappa from behind. This was limited curved fire, not homing or Yamcha’s Spirit Ball. Spirit Spear is recorded separately.

entry.title: Power suppression
entry.summary: Lowers emitted power and deliberately releases it for action.
entry.effect: Regulates how much ki is expressed and detectable.

trainingRecord.text: Self-taught in the chamber and checked with the scouter. The final test stayed near 1,538 through walking and a short combination, then returned deliberately to 3,075. Hard surprises can still cause spikes. Sleep and unconscious maintenance, perfect concealment and instant expert switching are not established. Suppression makes a given load harder; it does not multiply training gains. The opening soldier engagement demonstrated a deliberate full-power striking burst followed by a return to half output. At that historical base, half output was about 39,904; that calculation was not a new suppression check. Difficulty sensing a deeply suppressed opponent does not undo Zero’s own suppression skill.

uncontrolled-form.note: Involuntary manifestation. No voluntary mastery track is established.

entry.title: Uncontrolled Dark Factor
entry.summary: Releases the Dark Factor through an involuntary, dangerous manifestation.
entry.artworkAlt: Symbolic black-and-violet horned energy eruption for Uncontrolled Dark Factor.
entry.effect: The attachment can take control of Zero’s body; this is a witnessed manifestation, not a safe voluntary transformation.
entry.control: Chronoa’s seal contains it. Losing consciousness or nearing death with the channel open can trigger takeover. The failed Kaioken/channel test also triggered it while conscious: Kaioken collapsed and ×15 replaced ×10, without stacking.
entry.development: Containment remains intact; voluntary mastery has not been achieved.
entry.appearance: A dense black-and-violet mantle encloses body, hair and clothes, enlarging the silhouette with horn-like projections and pale claws. Reversion exposes the underlying clothes and injuries.

trainingRecord.text: Power erupted after a voice that felt like Zero’s own thoughts offered strength. Fighting Nappa felt dreamlike and apparently voluntary until the body turned toward a city against his wishes. Vegeta stopped him before he reached it. The dense mantle encloses his body, hair and clothes and slightly enlarges his silhouette; reversion reveals what was underneath without repairing battle damage. Its layered growling laugh is not a new technique. This is a recorded manifestation, not a safe transformation he can freely activate. A brief second takeover occurred during the 15 April Kaioken/channel test; Krillin stopped it immediately. Kaioken dropped out, so ×15 replaced the channel without stacking. Chronoa checked and settled the intact seal.

entry.title: Dark Factor Sealed Channel

entry.effect: Opens, regulates and closes the flow through Chronoa’s seal while retaining conscious control.

entry.development: Refining activation, sustained regulation and recovery between bouts.
entry.appearance: Pale violet aura and red irises, with ordinary physique and hair colour. The permanent seal is a black circle with four inward-curving hooks below the sternum. The icon is symbolic; the Character gallery carries the full appearance.

trainingRecord.text: Voluntary opening and closure developed through supervised practice. Full output reached three moving minutes during the first cleanup week; by 10 March the sequence ended without immediate leg trembling, but still left Zero winded and repeated attempts were tiring. No permanent absorption of the multiplier is established. If he loses consciousness or approaches death while channeling, Uncontrolled Dark Factor takes over: ×15 replaces ×10, rather than stacking. Ordinary sleep with the channel closed is safe. The seal contains the attachment; safe removal remains unresolved. The ability icon is symbolic; the character gallery retains the full appearance reference. Attempting Kaioken on top of the channel caused loss of control even while conscious. The seal itself remained intact after Chronoa’s check; separate channel use resumed. On Namek, Zero defeated Nappa while retaining control, then closed the flow before losing consciousness after Turles’s ambush. Later practice with Vegeta improved recovery without a new timed maximum.

trainingRecord.text: First achieved on 24 March, then developed through six weeks of instruction. Activation, release and movement are possible; no ×3 or higher factor is established. Stacking onto the opened seal triggered Uncontrolled Dark Factor on 15 April. That failed combination is not an available ×20 form. Four further weeks of instruction extended the moving demonstration to one minute. Guru’s release strengthened overall battle capacity, including resilience and endurance. Kaioken proficiency continued to develop through practice. A short ×2 burst injured Brask before his transformation. The latest week improved activation and release while moving; ×2 remains the demonstrated ceiling.

trainingRecord.text: King Kai’s exercises developed direction and short-range tracking during movement. Zero cannot read exact numbers, hidden reserves or deeply suppressed targets reliably. Familiarity and concentration matter; the scouter still supplies numerical readings. Later practice improved tracking familiar moving signatures without stopping to concentrate. Against Brask, close-range ki tracking helped counter a flash. Recent practice follows familiar and partially suppressed moving signatures; exact values still require the scouter.

trainingRecord.text: Zero named and first attempted it against Nappa on Namek. The first discharge scorched armour; the second tighter pulse breached a small section of already-damaged back armour and burned beneath it. It did not pierce through Nappa or become a sustained beam. The gathered charge is spent on release. During the latest week, a modest gathered charge became repeatable on a moving training approach and contact. The current technique profile records its ×2 regular release and mastery-dependent charge ceiling; those calibrations do not rewrite the earlier partial contacts.
